case_title: Abdul Jalil and others vs Md. Joynal Abedin and others
facts_summary: The plaintiffs sought specific performance of an unregistered contract for sale executed in 2006. The defendants contended that following the 2004 amendments introducing Section 54A in the Transfer of Property Act, Section 17A in the Registration Act, and Section 21A in the Specific Relief Act, no suit for specific performance lies on an unregistered contract for sale.
legal_issues: Whether an unregistered agreement for sale executed after the 2004 amendment can be enforced through a suit for specific performance in civil court.
ratio_decidendi: An agreement for sale of immovable property executed after the 2004 amendment must be compulsorily registered. An unregistered contract for sale is completely barred from being specifically enforced in civil court under Section 21A of the Specific Relief Act, 1877.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: By the amendment of 2004, the legislature has made registration of a contract for sale mandatory under section 17A of the Registration Act and section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act. Section 21A of the Specific Relief Act explicitly bars any court from entertaining a suit for specific performance of an unregistered contract for sale.

case_title: Md. Mozibur Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950

facts_summary: The dispute pertained to whether the record of rights (RS Khatian) published under Section 144 of the SAT Act creates title on its own in the absence of valid acquisition documents.
legal_issues: Whether a Khatian (Record of Rights) creates or extinguishes title to immovable property.
ratio_decidendi: A Khatian or Record of Rights (Porcha) does not create nor extinguish title to immovable property. It only raises a rebuttable presumption of possession and tenancy for revenue collection purposes under Section 144(4) of the SAT Act.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: It is well settled that entry in the record-of-rights does not create title. Record-of-rights is prepared for fiscal purposes, namely, collection of land revenue, and it raises only a rebuttable presumption of correctness regarding possession.

case_title: Md. Nurul Islam vs S.M. Shahjahan and others
facts_summary: Appeal against the grant of temporary injunction restraining the appellant from construction on disputed land during pendency of a partition suit.
legal_issues: What are the essential tripartite conditions governing the grant of temporary injunction under Order 39 of the CPC.
ratio_decidendi: To obtain a temporary injunction under Order 39, Rules 1 and 2 of the CPC, the applicant must establish all three conditions cumulatively: (1) a strong prima facie case, (2) irreparable loss and injury that cannot be compensated in money, and (3) balance of convenience in applicant's favour.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: An order of temporary injunction cannot be granted as a matter of course. The court must be satisfied on three indispensable ingredients: prima facie arguable case, balance of convenience and inconvenience, and irreparable injury.

case_title: Abdul Gafur vs Md. Shamsul Haque

governing_statutes.act_name: The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950

facts_summary: The pre-emptor filed an application for pre-emption under Section 96 of the SAT Act claiming rights as a co-sharer by inheritance. The vendee contended the applicant was only a co-sharer by purchase.
legal_issues: Whether a co-sharer by purchase holds statutory pre-emption rights after the 2006 amendment to Section 96 of the SAT Act.
ratio_decidendi: Following the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 2006 (Act No. 34 of 2006), the right of pre-emption under Section 96 is restricted strictly to a co-sharer by inheritance of the holding. A co-sharer by purchase or contiguous tenant has no right of pre-emption under Section 96.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: By the substituting amendment of section 96 in 2006, the legislature intentionally omitted contiguous land owners and co-sharers by purchase. Only a co-sharer in the holding by inheritance is entitled to maintain an application for pre-emption.

case_title: The State vs Md. Mofazzal Hossain
facts_summary: Application for anticipatory bail under Section 498 of CrPC in connection with an alleged financial dispute converted into a criminal complaint under Sections 406/420 of Penal Code.
legal_issues: What are the parameters for granting anticipatory bail under Section 498 CrPC in Bangladesh.
ratio_decidendi: Anticipatory bail under Section 498 CrPC is an extraordinary prerogative remedy granted only when there is reasonable apprehension of arrest with mala fide intent or where civil disputes are dressed up as criminal offences to cause harassment.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The power under section 498 of the Code to grant anticipatory bail is of an exceptional character. It must be exercised with caution where the petitioner establishes a prima facie apprehension of arrest based on motivated or frivolous accusations.

case_title: Government of Bangladesh vs Ayesha Khatun
facts_summary: Dispute concerning whether the children of a son who predeceased the grandfather are entitled to the full share their father would have inherited had he been alive at the opening of succession.
legal_issues: Whether Section 4 of MFLO 1961 overrides traditional Sharia rules of exclusion for orphaned grandchildren.
ratio_decidendi: Under Section 4 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, the children of any predeceased son or daughter inherit the exact per stirpes share which their parent would have received if alive at the time of the grandfather's death.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Section 4 of the Ordinance creates a statutory succession in favour of the children of a predeceased child. The succession opens on the death of the propositus and the children step into the shoes of their deceased parent per stirpes.

case_title: Khaleda Akter vs Md. Tariqul Islam
facts_summary: The wife filed a suit in Family Court for recovery of prompt and deferred dower (Denmohor) after divorce.
legal_issues: What is the limitation period for recovering prompt vs deferred dower under Bangladesh law.
ratio_decidendi: Prompt dower is payable on demand; limitation of 3 years runs from the date of demand and refusal under Article 103 of Limitation Act. Deferred dower becomes payable on dissolution of marriage by death or divorce; limitation runs 3 years from dissolution under Article 104.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Prompt dower is exigible on demand and limitation runs from the date of refusal. Deferred dower becomes due only on dissolution of the marriage by death or divorce, and the limitation is three years from the date of dissolution.

case_title: Md. Altaf Hossain vs The State and another
facts_summary: Petition under Section 561A CrPC to quash criminal proceedings initiated on a breach of contract regarding supply of construction materials.
legal_issues: When can the High Court Division exercise inherent powers under Section 561A CrPC to quash criminal proceedings arising from contractual breach.
ratio_decidendi: Mere breach of contract does not give rise to criminal prosecution for cheating or criminal breach of trust under Sections 406/420 of Penal Code unless fraudulent intention is shown at the inception of the transaction. Criminal proceedings used as a tool of coercion for civil debt recovery must be quashed under Section 561A CrPC to prevent abuse of the process of the court.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: To constitute an offence of cheating under section 420, dishonest intention must exist at the inception of the contract. Where the allegations disclose only a civil liability, criminal proceedings cannot be permitted as a coercive tool.

case_title: Md. Sirajul Islam vs Begum Feroza Sultana
facts_summary: Suit for specific performance of contract for sale where the purchaser delayed payment and subsequently filed suit after escalation of land prices.
legal_issues: Whether the jurisdiction to decree specific performance under Section 22 of Specific Relief Act is discretionary and whether readiness and willingness must be proven continuously.
ratio_decidendi: Specific performance is a discretionary relief under Section 22 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. The plaintiff must prove readiness and willingness to perform their part of the contract from the date of the contract continuously up to the date of hearing.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The jurisdiction to decree specific performance is discretionary, and the court is not bound to grant such relief merely because it is lawful to do so. The plaintiff must aver and prove that he was always ready and willing to perform his essential obligations.

case_title: Haji Md. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh and others
facts_summary: The plaintiff filed a suit seeking bare declaration of title under Section 42 of Specific Relief Act without praying for recovery of khas possession, although the plaintiff was completely out of possession.
legal_issues: Whether a suit for bare declaration of title is maintainable without seeking consequential relief of possession under the proviso to Section 42 of Specific Relief Act.
ratio_decidendi: Under the proviso to Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877, no court shall make a declaration where the plaintiff, being able to seek further relief such as recovery of possession, omits to do so. A suit for bare declaration by a plaintiff out of possession is barred.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act is mandatory. When the plaintiff is out of possession and in a position to claim recovery of possession, a suit for simple declaration of title is hit by the proviso and must be dismissed.

case_title: Md. Shahidul Islam vs Md. Anowar Hossain
facts_summary: Application by defendant for rejection of plaint under Order 7 Rule 11 of CPC on the ground that the suit was barred by limitation on the face of the plaint averments.
legal_issues: What materials can the court examine when deciding an application for rejection of plaint under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC.
ratio_decidendi: For deciding an application under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC, the court must look strictly and exclusively at the averments in the plaint. The defense set up in the written statement or annexures cannot be considered at that stage.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: For the purpose of deciding an application under Order VII, Rule 11 of the Code, only the plaint averments are material. The court cannot look into the written statement or extraneous materials submitted by the defendant.

case_title: Md. Lokman vs State
facts_summary: Criminal appeal challenging conviction on the ground that the FIR omitted the names of eyewitnesses and specific weapon roles.
legal_issues: Whether the First Information Report (FIR) is substantive evidence and whether omission of minute details is fatal to prosecution.
ratio_decidendi: An FIR is not a substantive piece of evidence; it can only be used to corroborate or contradict its maker under the Evidence Act. An FIR is not required to be an encyclopedia of the entire incident.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The First Information Report is not an encyclopaedia of the prosecution case. It is only information of a cognizable offence to set the criminal law into motion. Non-mention of minute details does not vitiate the prosecution case.

case_title: Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST) and others vs Bangladesh and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Public interest litigation challenging widespread misuse of police powers of arrest without warrant under Section 54 and detention on remand under Section 167 CrPC violating constitutional safeguards.
legal_issues: Whether the police can arrest without warrant under Section 54 CrPC and obtain magistrate detention/remand under Section 167 CrPC without adhering to mandatory constitutional protections under Articles 31, 32, 33, and 35.
ratio_decidendi: Lays down mandatory 15-point operational guidelines for arrest without warrant under Section 54 and interrogation/remand under Section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Reaffirms that detention cannot exceed 24 hours without production before a Magistrate under Section 61 CrPC and Article 33 of the Constitution, and strictly prohibits physical or psychological torture during remand under Article 35(5).

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Section 54 and section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure must be read strictly in conformity with the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 27, 31, 32, 33 and 35 of the Constitution. No person arrested without warrant shall be detained in custody for a period exceeding twenty-four hours without the authority of a Magistrate, and no accused shall be subjected to torture in custody.

case_title: Md. Harun-or-Rashid vs Monowara Begum and others
facts_summary: Challenge to an alleged oral Hiba (gift) of land made after the 2004 amendment to the Registration Act.
legal_issues: Whether an oral Hiba of immovable property between Muslims remains valid without a registered instrument after 2004.
ratio_decidendi: Following the 2004 amendment to Section 17(1) of the Registration Act, 1908, a declaration of Hiba (gift) under Muslim law regarding immovable property must be made through a registered instrument. An unregistered oral Hiba confers no legal title.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: By inserting clause (aa) in section 17(1) of the Registration Act in 2004, the legislature has brought an end to oral Hiba of immovable property. Registration of an instrument of declaration of Hiba is now compulsory.

case_title: Md. Abul Hossain vs Md. Habibur Rahman
facts_summary: Plaintiff sought to amend the plaint after commencement of trial to introduce an entirely new cause of action changing the fundamental character of the suit.
legal_issues: What are the limitations on allowing amendment of pleadings under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC after trial has commenced.
ratio_decidendi: Amendments under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC should be allowed liberally for determining real questions in controversy, provided the amendment does not introduce a completely new inconsistent cause of action or alter the fundamental character of the suit.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The power to amend pleadings is aimed at serving the ends of justice. However, an amendment which changes the fundamental nature and character of the suit or introduces a time-barred claim cannot be allowed.

case_title: Abdul Khaleque vs Mrs. Feroza Begum
facts_summary: Suit for cancellation of a registered deed of sale obtained through fraudulent impersonation.
legal_issues: When does limitation begin for a suit to cancel a fraudulent instrument under Section 39 of Specific Relief Act and Article 91 of Limitation Act.
ratio_decidendi: In a suit for cancellation of a fraudulent deed under Section 39 of the Specific Relief Act, the 3-year limitation period under Article 91 of the Limitation Act begins to run from the date the plaintiff discovers the facts entitling them to have the instrument cancelled.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Under Article 91 of the Limitation Act, time runs from the date when the facts entitling the plaintiff to have the instrument cancelled or set aside become known to him, and not from the date of registration of the fraudulent deed.

case_title: Md. Rashedul Islam vs The State
facts_summary: Application for bail where the accused was in custody for 3 years without trial commencement in a non-capital offence.
legal_issues: Whether prolonged custody without trial constitutes a valid ground for granting bail under Section 498 CrPC.
ratio_decidendi: Inordinate and unexplained delay in trial resulting in prolonged pre-trial detention violates the constitutional right to speedy trial under Article 35(3) and constitutes a valid and compelling ground for granting bail under Section 498 CrPC.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Indefinite detention of an undertrial prisoner without any fault on his part amounts to pre-trial punishment. Prolonged detention without trial is a legitimate ground for granting bail under section 498 of the Code.

case_title: Fazlul Haque vs Md. Enamul Haque
facts_summary: Defendant pleaded Res Judicata on the ground that the issue of title was previously decided in an earlier suit between the same parties.
legal_issues: Conditions required to bar a subsequent suit under Section 11 of the CPC (Doctrine of Res Judicata).
ratio_decidendi: To attract Section 11 CPC, the matter directly and substantially in issue in the subsequent suit must have been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, heard and finally decided by a court of competent jurisdiction.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Res Judicata is founded on public policy to prevent multiplicity of litigation. The identity of the subject-matter, the parties, the title, and final adjudication by a competent court are sine qua non for applying section 11.

case_title: Yaor Mia (Md) and another vs Haji Shah Dhanai Ali and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950

facts_summary: Suit concerning the interaction between land transfer under the Transfer of Property Act and subsequent revenue mutation under the SAT Act.
legal_issues: Relationship between title acquisition by transfer deed and administrative rent-roll mutation under SAT Act.
ratio_decidendi: Mutation of a holding in revenue records does not determine title to immovable property. Title passes upon execution and registration of the deed; mutation is an administrative recording of the taxpayer liable for rent.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Mutation of names in the revenue record is only for the purpose of payment of rent and does not confer any title. Title to immovable property is governed by the substantive law of transfer and valid conveyance.

case_title: Mrs. Nasreen Akhter vs Bangladesh and others
facts_summary: Mother sought custody of her minor children after divorce; the father contended traditional Hizanat age limits had expired.
legal_issues: Whether the welfare of the minor child overrides rigid statutory age rules in determining custody.
ratio_decidendi: In child custody disputes under Section 17 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, the welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration, which overrides rigid traditional age thresholds of maternal custody (Hizanat).

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The welfare of the minor is of paramount importance in deciding custody. The rules of personal law regarding the age of Hizanat are subordinate to the welfare and moral wellbeing of the minor child.

case_title: Md. Mokhlesur Rahman vs Md. Habibur Rahman and others
facts_summary: Challenge to a sale deed registered without the seller holding an updated mutation Khatian in his name.
legal_issues: Effect of non-compliance with Section 52A of the Registration Act, 1908 on the validity of deed registration.
ratio_decidendi: Under Section 52A of the Registration Act, 1908, the Sub-Registrar is legally mandated to refuse registration of a sale deed unless the seller presents an updated mutation Khatian and proof of land development tax payment in the seller's name.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Section 52A was inserted in 2004 to eliminate fraudulent transfers. A seller who is not recorded in the latest Khatian and has not paid land development tax cannot execute a valid registered conveyance.

case_title: Haji Md. Aslam vs Md. Shafiqul Islam
facts_summary: Vendor claimed contract for sale was rescinded because the buyer failed to pay the balance within the stipulated 6 months.
legal_issues: Whether time is of the essence of contract in transactions relating to sale of immovable property in Bangladesh.
ratio_decidendi: In contracts for the sale of immovable property, time is presumed not to be of the essence unless there is an express contractual stipulation or surrounding circumstances showing an intention to make time strictly essential.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: In agreements for sale of immovable property, fixation of a period for completion does not per se make time the essence of the contract. The intention to make time essential must be clear from the terms or conduct of the parties.

case_title: Mrs. Shima Rani Das vs Narayan Chandra Das and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act, 1937

facts_summary: Hindu widow claimed partition of her deceased husband's share in joint family agricultural and residential property.
legal_issues: What is the extent of a Hindu widow's life interest in her deceased husband's property under the 1937 Act in Bangladesh.
ratio_decidendi: Under Section 3 of the Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act, 1937, a Hindu widow inherits the same share as her deceased husband in joint family property, holding a limited life estate with the right to claim partition during her lifetime.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The 1937 Act confers upon the widow the same interest in the property as her husband had. Though it is a limited interest known as Hindu Women's Estate, she is fully competent to seek partition of the holding.

case_title: Md. Rafiqul Islam vs Government of Bangladesh
facts_summary: Revision petition challenging an appellate court's concurrent finding of fact without pointing to any jurisdictional error.
legal_issues: Scope and limits of revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Section 115 of the CPC.
ratio_decidendi: Revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 CPC is restricted to jurisdictional errors, illegal exercise, or material irregularity. The High Court Division cannot sit as a court of second appeal to re-appreciate concurrent findings of fact.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Section 115 of the Code is limited to rectifying errors of jurisdiction. It is not an appellate power and the High Court Division cannot interfere with findings of fact unless they are perverse or based on no evidence.

case_title: Eastern Bank Limited vs Md. Shafiuddin and others
facts_summary: Bank initiated auction of mortgaged property under Section 12 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain without following mandatory pre-auction publication requirements.
legal_issues: Whether the procedure for private auction under Section 12 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain is mandatory before filing an Artha Rin suit.
ratio_decidendi: The requirement of attempting sale of mortgaged property under Section 12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 prior to filing a money claim is mandatory. Any deviation renders subsequent recovery proceedings defective.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Section 12 of the Ain mandates that the financial institution must make earnest efforts to sell the mortgaged security by auction before approaching the court. Compliance with this provision is a statutory prerequisite.

case_title: Secretary, Ministry of Finance vs Md. Masdar Hossain and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Judicial officers filed a writ petition seeking judicial independence and separation of the subordinate judiciary from the executive branch in accordance with Article 22 of the Constitution.
legal_issues: Whether the subordinate judiciary must be structurally and administratively separated from the executive branch under the Constitution of Bangladesh.
ratio_decidendi: Separation of the judiciary from the executive organs of the State is a basic pillar and constitutional mandate under Article 22. Subordinate courts must be under the exclusive administrative control and superintendence of the Supreme Court under Article 116.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The separation of the judiciary from the executive organs of the State is the basic feature of the Constitution. The judicial service is distinct and separate from civil executive services and must be administered independently under the superintendence of the Supreme Court.

case_title: Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST) and others vs Bangladesh and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Following the custodial death of student Shamim Reza Rubel after arbitrary arrest under Section 54 of CrPC, human rights organizations challenged arbitrary police powers of arrest without warrant and remand under Section 167.
legal_issues: Whether police officers have unfettered discretion to arrest without warrant under Section 54 CrPC and whether magistrate can routinely grant police remand under Section 167 without recording reasons.
ratio_decidendi: Arrest under Section 54 CrPC requires credible information and reasonable suspicion, not arbitrary whim. Police must disclose identity, inform relatives within 3 hours, and magistrates cannot grant police remand mechanically without hearing the accused and recording cogent legal grounds.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not give arbitrary or unbridled power to a police officer to arrest anyone on simple suspicion. The Magistrate must strictly follow guidelines before granting detention in police custody under Section 167.

case_title: Md. Humayun Kabir vs State and another
facts_summary: Complainant filed a case under Section 138 of NI Act before the expiry of the mandatory 15-day payment window following receipt of the legal notice.
legal_issues: Whether a criminal complaint under Section 138 of NI Act is maintainable if filed prematurely prior to the expiry of 15 days from notice receipt.
ratio_decidendi: The statutory sequence under Section 138 of the NI Act is mandatory. Cause of action arises only after the drawer fails to make payment within 15 days of receiving the legal notice. A complaint filed before expiration of this 15-day period is premature and must be quashed.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: No cause of action arises to file a petition of complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act before the expiry of 15 days from the date of receipt of the legal notice. Premature filing renders the proceeding void ab initio.

case_title: Syed Farhad Hossain vs State and another
facts_summary: A director of a private limited company was prosecuted under Section 138 of NI Act for a cheque issued on behalf of the company without specific averment that he was in charge of the conduct of the business.
legal_issues: Whether an ordinary director can be held vicariously liable under Section 141 of NI Act without specific averments in the complaint.
ratio_decidendi: Under Section 141 of NI Act, vicarious criminal liability requires clear and specific averment in the complaint showing that the director was in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business at the time the offence was committed.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: To fasten vicarious liability under Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, there must be a specific assertion in the petition of complaint as to how and in what manner the concerned director was responsible for the conduct of the business of the company.

case_title: KAFCO vs Karnaphuli Fertilizer Company Limited and others
facts_summary: Dispute arose regarding interim relief granted by civil court in a dispute where arbitration seat was located outside Bangladesh.
legal_issues: Whether the District Court has jurisdiction to grant interim measures of protection under Section 7A of the Arbitration Act, 2001 in an international commercial arbitration seated outside Bangladesh.
ratio_decidendi: Following the 2004 amendment adding Section 7A to the Arbitration Act 2001, civil courts in Bangladesh have statutory jurisdiction to grant interim measures of protection even if the place of arbitration is outside Bangladesh.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Section 7A of the Arbitration Act, 2001 confers specific power on the court to grant interim protective orders in international commercial arbitration, irrespective of whether the arbitral seat is located within or outside the territory of Bangladesh.

case_title: Unimarine S.A. vs Bangladesh Bank and others
facts_summary: A foreign shipping company sought enforcement of a foreign arbitral award rendered in London under Section 45 of Arbitration Act 2001.
legal_issues: What are the narrow grounds for refusing recognition and execution of a foreign arbitral award under Section 46 of Arbitration Act, 2001.
ratio_decidendi: Foreign arbitral awards under the New York Convention must be enforced as a decree of the court under Section 45. Recognition can only be refused on the exhaustive grounds in Section 46, such as public policy violation or invalidity of arbitration agreement.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The grounds for refusal of recognition and execution of a foreign arbitral award under Section 46 of the Act of 2001 are exhaustive. The court cannot sit as an appellate court to review the merits of the arbitral tribunal's determination.

case_title: Mahbuba Huq vs Dr. Syed Moinuddin Hossain
facts_summary: Husband argued that claim for prompt dower filed after 10 years of marriage was barred by limitation under Article 103 of Limitation Act.
legal_issues: When does limitation begin to run against a Muslim wife seeking recovery of prompt dower (Mu'ajjal) during the subsistence of marriage.
ratio_decidendi: Prompt dower is payable immediately upon demand. Limitation under Article 103 of the Limitation Act runs only from the date when prompt dower is demanded and refused, or when marriage is dissolved. Non-demand during marriage creates no limitation bar.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Prompt dower becomes payable upon demand. So long as there is no formal demand by the wife and refusal by the husband, limitation under Article 103 does not begin to run during the subsistence of the conjugal relationship.

case_title: Md. Rafiqul Islam vs Government of Bangladesh and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: A petitioner sought a Writ of Mandamus compelling public authority to perform mandatory statutory duties regarding land mutation settlement.
legal_issues: What are the prerequisites for issuing a Writ of Mandamus under Article 102(2)(a)(i) of the Constitution.
ratio_decidendi: A Writ of Mandamus will lie to compel a public authority to perform a mandatory duty imposed by statute, provided the petitioner has a legal right to performance and has made a prior demand for justice which was refused or ignored.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Mandamus is an extraordinary constitutional remedy to enforce a public legal duty. Where a statutory authority fails or refuses to perform its statutory obligations, the High Court Division under Article 102 has jurisdiction to compel compliance.

case_title: Abdul Quader Mollah vs Chief Prosecutor

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Convict challenged government's right of appeal against inadequacy of sentence following 2013 statutory amendment to Section 21 of Act of 1973.
legal_issues: Whether procedural statutory amendments creating a right of appeal apply retrospectively to pending judicial matters under special tribunals.
ratio_decidendi: Amendments touching purely upon procedural rights, such as creating a right of appeal for the prosecution against inadequacy of sentence, operate retrospectively and apply to pending proceedings unless explicitly barred by statute.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: An amendment in procedural law is retrospective in operation and applies to pending proceedings unless the legislature has expressed a contrary intention.

case_title: Ain O Salish Kendra (ASK) vs Government of Bangladesh

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Public interest litigation challenging forceful, unannounced eviction of slum dwellers without rehabilitation plans.
legal_issues: Whether the constitutional right to life under Article 32 encompasses the right to livelihood and protection from arbitrary eviction without rehabilitation.
ratio_decidendi: The right to life guaranteed under Article 32 includes the right to livelihood. The state cannot arbitrarily evict slum dwellers without reasonable notice and an opportunity for basic relocation or rehabilitation.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Right to life under Article 32 of the Constitution does not mean mere animal existence. It includes the right to live with human dignity and livelihood. Eviction without prior notice and rehabilitation violates constitutional safeguards.

case_title: Kazi Mukhlesur Rahman vs Bangladesh

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: An advocate challenged the Delhi Treaty / Berubari border demarcation agreement between Bangladesh and India on constitutional grounds.
legal_issues: Whether an individual citizen has locus standi under Article 102 to challenge international boundary treaties affecting the nation's territory.
ratio_decidendi: Where a constitutional question of grave public importance arises affecting the territory or governance of the Republic, any citizen has locus standi to invoke the writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: When a question involves the constitutional validity of a treaty ceding territory of the Republic, any citizen has a sufficient interest to maintain a petition under Article 102 of the Constitution.

case_title: Haji Md. Shamsul Alam vs Commissioner of Customs and others
facts_summary: Customs authority confiscated imported goods and imposed penalty without serving proper show cause notice under Section 180 of Customs Act.
legal_issues: Whether compliance with natural justice and notice requirements under Section 180 of Customs Act is mandatory prior to confiscation.
ratio_decidendi: Section 180 of the Customs Act, 1969 mandates that no order of confiscation or penalty can be made without giving the owner of goods written notice stating the grounds and a reasonable opportunity of making representation.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The requirement of serving a show-cause notice under Section 180 of the Customs Act is a statutory embodiment of natural justice. Any adjudication order passed in violation thereof is null and void.

case_title: Dr. Shirin Akhtar vs Ministry of Land and others

governing_statutes.act_name: Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Act, 2017
The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Land owner challenged government acquisition where possession was forcibly taken before payment of statutory compensation.
legal_issues: Whether the government can take physical possession of acquired private land before assessing and paying compensation to lawful title-holders.
ratio_decidendi: Under property acquisition laws and Article 42 of the Constitution, statutory compensation must be determined and disbursed before taking possession of private land for public purpose.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The State cannot dispossess a citizen of private property under the colour of acquisition without strictly complying with the statutory requirement of prior assessment and payment of compensation.

case_title: Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA) vs Ministry of Environment

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: BELA challenged unapproved industrial projects and ship-breaking yards operating in ecologically critical coastal zones.
legal_issues: Whether industrial and commercial activities can operate without Environmental Clearance Certificates under Section 12 of ECA 1995.
ratio_decidendi: Article 18A of the Constitution imposes an affirmative constitutional duty on the State to protect the environment. No commercial entity can operate in an ecologically critical zone without a valid Environmental Clearance Certificate.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Protection of the environment under Article 18A is a constitutional obligation. The Precautionary Principle and Polluter Pays Principle form part of the environmental jurisprudence of Bangladesh.

case_title: Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh and others
facts_summary: High Court Division reversed an order of acquittal passed by trial court without finding compelling and substantial reasons.
legal_issues: What is the standard for an appellate court when reversing a judgment of acquittal under Section 417 of CrPC.
ratio_decidendi: An order of acquittal strengthens the initial presumption of innocence. An appellate court should not interfere with an acquittal merely because an alternative view is possible; interference requires perverse or illegal findings by the trial court.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: In an appeal against acquittal under Section 417 of the Code, the appellate court must exercise caution. If the view taken by the trial judge is a reasonably plausible view on the evidence, the acquittal cannot be reversed.

case_title: Rashida Khatun vs Md. Kamal Hossain
facts_summary: Wife filed criminal complaint alleging dowry demand based on customary wedding gifts exchanged during marriage ceremony.
legal_issues: Whether voluntary gifts presented at the time of marriage constitute 'dowry' under the Dowry Prohibition Act.
ratio_decidendi: Dowry demands require a coercive condition for marriage or continuation of marital life. Voluntary traditional gifts given without demand or coercion do not fall within the penal definition of dowry under the Act.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: To constitute dowry under the Act, property or valuable security must be demanded as consideration for the marriage. Customary gifts voluntarily presented without demand cannot form the basis of a criminal prosecution.

case_title: Al-Arafah Islami Bank Ltd vs M/S R.R. Trading and others
facts_summary: Dispute concerning issuance of ownership certificate to decree-holder financial institution under Section 33(7) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain.
legal_issues: Whether a certificate under Section 33(7) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain vests absolute title and right to possession in the decree-holder bank.
ratio_decidendi: When mortgaged property remains unsold after successive auctions in execution, a certificate issued under Section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 vests absolute title in the decree-holder bank, entitling it to seek immediate delivery of possession through court.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Upon issuance of a certificate under Section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the right, title, and interest in the mortgaged property vest completely in the decree-holder financial institution.

case_title: Md. Sohel Rana vs State
facts_summary: Bail petition of commercial building owner following the structural collapse of Rana Plaza causing mass casualties.
legal_issues: Whether knowingly operating a structurally defective multi-storey building with heavy industrial generators constitutes culpable homicide under Section 304 of Penal Code.
ratio_decidendi: Operating unauthorized heavy commercial machinery in a visibly fractured building with knowledge that it is likely to cause death falls within Section 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) rather than mere rash and negligent act under Section 304A.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Where a person has knowledge of structural cracks and continues to force workers into the building, the element of knowledge under Section 304 Part II of the Penal Code is attracted, taking it out of the purview of simple negligence.

case_title: Khandaker Delwar Hossain vs Bangladesh Italian Marble Works Ltd

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Constitutional challenge to the Constitution (Fifth Amendment) Act, 1979 validating martial law proclamations between 1975 and 1979.
legal_issues: Whether the Constitution can be amended or suspended by extra-constitutional Martial Law Proclamations.
ratio_decidendi: The Constitution is the supreme law of the Republic under Article 7. Extra-constitutional takeover and martial law proclamations are ultra vires, void ab initio, and cannot be validated by subsequent constitutional amendments.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: The Constitution of Bangladesh is the supreme law and nobody is above it. Taking over power by extra-constitutional means and suspending the Constitution is treason and void ab initio.

case_title: Government of Bangladesh vs Advocate Asaduzzaman Siddiqui and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Challenge to the Constitution (Sixteenth Amendment) Act, 2014 restoring parliamentary power to remove Supreme Court judges.
legal_issues: Whether parliamentary removal of judges destroys judicial independence and violates the basic structure of the Constitution.
ratio_decidendi: Judicial independence is part of the inviolable basic structure of the Constitution. Empowering Parliament to remove judges on grounds of misconduct breaches separation of powers; the Supreme Judicial Council mechanism under Article 96 is essential for safeguarding judicial tenure.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Independence of the judiciary is a fundamental pillar of the Constitution. Subjecting superior court judges to parliamentary removal impairs judicial independence and violates the basic structure of our constitutional framework.

case_title: Grameenphone Ltd vs Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC)
facts_summary: Telecommunications operator filed a civil title suit and sought an injunction against BTRC's administrative audit claim of BDT 12,579 crore.
legal_issues: Whether a civil court can stay an administrative audit demand by a statutory regulator without requiring a security deposit.
ratio_decidendi: In substantial revenue and regulatory audit disputes, the grant of an interlocutory injunction staying public revenue demands must be balanced with the public interest by requiring an equitable deposit.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: When staying a statutory regulatory demand involving public revenue under Order 39 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court must balance the balance of convenience with public interest by directing a reasonable interim deposit.

case_title: Anowara Begum vs Md. Nurul Islam and others
facts_summary: Dispute between heirs over an oral gift (Hiba) executed prior to the 2004 amendment requiring compulsory registration of Hiba instruments.
legal_issues: What are the mandatory elements of a valid Hiba under Muslim personal law for transactions executed prior to 2004.
ratio_decidendi: For gifts executed prior to the 2004 statutory registration amendment, three essential elements must be proven to constitute a valid Muslim Hiba: (1) declaration of gift by donor, (2) acceptance by donee, and (3) complete delivery of actual or constructive possession.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Under Mahomedan Law, three conditions are necessary for a valid gift (Hiba): declaration of the gift by the donor, acceptance of the gift by the donee, and delivery of possession of the subject matter. Without delivery of possession, the gift is invalid.

case_title: Shamsun Nahar vs Principal, Holy Cross College and others

governing_statutes.act_name: The Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh

facts_summary: Writ petition challenging arbitrary exclusion of students from sitting public examinations based on internal college disciplinary guidelines.
legal_issues: Whether educational institutions receiving government approval can arbitrarily debar students without reasonable cause and natural justice.
ratio_decidendi: Access to education and participation in public board examinations are fundamental aspects of protection under law. Educational institutions cannot act arbitrarily without conforming to the principles of natural justice and fair notice.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Educational authorities must exercise discretion fairly and transparently. Denying a student the right to sit in public examinations without granting an opportunity of being heard violates Article 27 and 31 of the Constitution.

case_title: Robi Axiata Limited vs Commissioner of Large Taxpayers Unit (LTU-VAT)
facts_summary: Dispute on whether SIM replacement without change of subscriber connection is subject to VAT and SIM tax under the Value Added Tax Act.
legal_issues: Whether the issuance of a replacement SIM for an existing connection constitutes a taxable supply under Section 3 of the VAT Act.
ratio_decidendi: Taxing statutes must be construed strictly. In the absence of express statutory charging language taxing replacement of defective SIMs, administrative circulars cannot create a tax liability beyond the four corners of the Act.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: In a taxing statute, one has to look merely at what is clearly said. There is no room for any intendment. Subjecting SIM replacement to tax without an explicit legislative charge is impermissible.

case_title: Md. Jahangir Alam vs Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) and another
facts_summary: Accused challenged prosecution under Section 27(1) of ACC Act for alleged disproportionate assets on grounds that initial wealth notice was defective.
legal_issues: What constitutes proof of disproportionate assets under Section 27(1) of Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004.
ratio_decidendi: Once the prosecution establishes that a public servant is in possession of pecuniary resources or property disproportionate to their known sources of lawful income, the statutory burden shifts to the accused under Section 27(1) to satisfactorily account for the same.

exact_key_passages.quote_text: Under Section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, when the prosecution proves that the assets are disproportionate to known sources of income, the burden shifts to the accused to satisfactorily account for how the wealth was acquired.
